solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: M-Man, perhaps with plaster for 13

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000
the Isle of Man is one example of a body of land surrounded by sea, so 'perhaps' marks it as an instance
a sticking plaster is a bandage put on a wound

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with a thousand-man workforce reaches for a plaster, as if the clue were about a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is SALAD, so 'for 13' defines something you put on a salad. The Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink mayonnaise-based sauce is a classic topping poured over leaves, so it is something meant for salad.

clue.text: It flipped and croaked as ordered

indicators.note: flipped means the word it is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: croaked is slang for expired, passed away

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a frog, turned over and gave up the ghost on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns IT into TI; 'croaked' looks like a frog's noise but is slang for died.
explanation.definitionFit: A room that has been ordered has been put straight and made neat, a synonym.

clue.text: Solver briefly tours port, having got up at an unspecified time

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the whole assembly is read from the bottom upwards
tours means going round, so one piece encloses the other
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you by the setter
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: The puzzle-solver visits a harbour after rising, on some vague occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solver' is the setter addressing you. Aden is a port in Yemen. 'having got up' reverses the whole assembly, YADENO, because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at some point in the future or past, a time left vague.

clue.text: In psychoanalysis, although made of strong fibre

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A remark about therapy that suddenly turns to talk of tough material.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'psychoanalysis' into 'although'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is the tough fibre from an agave leaf, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Piece of music with oboist solo on, even only at the last minute

parts.note: a nonet is a composition for nine players

indicators.note: nothing in the clue truly signals that the odd letters of oboist are taken; 'with' is the nearest word, and the setter left this step unmarked
even picks the even-numbered letters of each of the two words solo and on

explanation.surface: A composition with an oboe solo, performed just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: A flawed clue: 'even' gives OO from solo and N from on, but the odd letters OOS of oboist have no signal at all; the blogger and commenters agreed the instruction is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving barely in time, almost too late, is the idiom's sense: it came, but only just.

clue.text: See 1
Off to bars? Yes and no

definitions.text: Off to bars? Yes and no

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether they are heading out to the pub, someone answers with a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges the letters of TO BARS and YES. Read whole, the clue describes going to the bars (yes) but not drinking (no).
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pub but not drinking is both visiting bars and abstaining, which keeps one clear-headed.

clue.text: To be as subtle, perhaps, is truly superlative

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A claim that subtlety is the finest quality anyone could have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the twelve letters of TO BE AS SUBTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbeatable is the very top of its kind, the highest possible, which is what superlative means.

clue.text: Scoffing riders, essentially doing what they do

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the very centre of the word riders

parts.note: what riders do is sit on and control horses or bikes

explanation.surface: Mocking horsemen while they are simply getting on with their job.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of RIDERS is DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffing means mocking or jeering, a straight synonym of the participle.

clue.text: See 1
It's sad that artist main comeback is in album by Cardini

indicators.note: is in means the reversed run sits inside the other piece

parts.note: CD is compact disc, an album format

indicators.note: comeback means the three pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the main is a poetic name for the open ocean

explanation.surface: A lament that a painter's big return appears on a record by someone called Cardini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reverses all three pieces together, giving AESARSALA. Caesar Cardini, an Italian-American restaurateur, is credited with inventing the dish in Tijuana, so 'by Cardini' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The romaine and anchovy dish is named after its creator, the Tijuana restaurateur Caesar Cardini, so it is a creation by him.

clue.text: See 7
Eastern writer unwrapping one of his missives for decoration

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
St Paul wrote many epistles in the New Testament

indicators.note: unwrapping means taking off the outside, the first and last letters

parts.note: Paul's missives are his epistles, each of them a letter

explanation.surface: Someone from the East opens a note from a correspondent and finds a gift of ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapping' strips L and R from LETTER to leave ETTE. 'writer' is the apostle Paul, author of the epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform, a decoration worn on the coat.

clue.text: See 10
Right away, leader of municipality and county clinic is allowed to love 9

indicators.note: away means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a mayor heads a town council

explanation.surface: A garbled civic notice about a mayor, a county and a hospital, with romance thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is DRESSING. The clue also hides further hints: Mayo is an Irish county, the Mayo Clinic a US hospital, and MAY (is allowed) plus O (love) also builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is the everyday short form of mayonnaise, a sauce poured or spread on salads.

clue.text: It's doubtful anyone can bother

indicators.note: doubtful means uncertain, so the letters are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrug: it's not certain that anybody can be bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubtful' rearranges ANYONE CAN; 'bother' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother as a noun is irritation or nuisance, a synonym.

clue.text: I am fairly confident in brown Asian

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
I bet is a way of saying I'm pretty sure

explanation.surface: Someone is fairly sure that a brown-skinned person comes from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am fairly confident' is the spoken phrase 'I bet', which supplies four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tibet, a region of the Himalayas, is an Asian, so the noun is a specific example.

clue.text: 13 and loveless — big bum

parts.note: big means fat

indicators.note: and adds the missing love back into the other two words, cutting them open

parts.note: tush is slang, chiefly American, for the backside
the clue runs backwards: the answer without love, the tennis zero, gives the words that follow, so love has to be put back in

explanation.surface: A crude remark that salad without love leads to a large backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: remove O (love, the tennis zero) from the answer and FAT TUSH remains, so the solver puts O into FAT TUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: This Levantine bread-and-vegetable mix of toasted pitta, herbs and sumac is a salad.

clue.text: Porter's rule 13

parts.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter, so Porter's points to his first name with a possessive S
a rule is a law

explanation.surface: A reference to some regulation laid down by a doorman or a famous composer.
explanation.walkthrough: COLE'S LAW, a joke rule of the composer Cole Porter, reads as the shredded-cabbage dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded raw cabbage and carrot in mayonnaise is a salad, served as a side dish.

clue.text: Spring in Athens is plentiful

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the city is read as 'A then S', the letter A followed by the letter S
to spring is to leap or jump forward

explanation.surface: Springtime in the Greek capital is a season of abundance.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to read 'Athens' as 'A then S': BOUND (spring) goes in A then S.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in great numbers, so the verb means occurs in plenty.

clue.text: See 4
Change for Emma after a bath and deodorant?

indicators.note: washing and deodorant take away BO, body odour, so those letters go

parts.note: Emma Bovary is the heroine of Flaubert's novel Madame Bovary

explanation.surface: A suggestion that Emma might be a new woman after freshening up.
explanation.walkthrough: BO is body odour. Emma is Flaubert's Madame Bovary, so remove BO from BOVARY.
explanation.definitionFit: To vary is to alter or become different, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: See 22
13 9 indecently lead on a virgin

indicators.note: indecently suggests improper behaviour, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A sordid tale of someone leading a virgin astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 9 is SALAD DRESSING; 'indecently' rearranges LEAD ON A VIRGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinaigrette made from these two liquids is the classic simple dressing for greens.

clue.text: Sway in to get the guard

parts.note: the word is split as the letter S followed by way; the S is kept and way joins the next word
together with the way from the previous word, way in means an entrance or doorway

explanation.surface: Someone is told to persuade their way in, to get round security.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Sway' as S plus 'way', and 'way in' is ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted to keep watch at a gate is a guard, a synonym.

clue.text: Minute from St Leger, only every second counts

indicators.note: every second means only the second, fourth and so on of each word's letters are used

explanation.surface: A racing commentator stresses that at the St Leger, a classic horse race, each moment matters.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every second letter of each word separately: sT, lEgEr, oNlY. The St Leger is an English horse race at Doncaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute pronounced my-NEWT means extremely small, and the answer is a childish word for tiny.

clue.text: One might like red mobile phone to be dropped in uncovered toilet

indicators.note: dropped in means placed inside the other piece
uncovered means the first and last letters are stripped from the word toilet
mobile means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A familiar mishap: a red mobile phone falls into a toilet with no lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' makes ENOPH; 'red' here is wine, not the phone's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur of wine would be expected to enjoy red, so the definition is a cryptic example.

clue.text: Not what comes up in rhymes or poetry

definitions.text: Not what comes up in rhymes or poetry

indicators.note: comes up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A literary remark about what doesn't turn up in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'Not what' as the definition, but it does not stand alone; the whole clue defines the answer. In a down entry 'comes up' reads ESORP, hidden in 'rhymes or poetry', from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary written language without metre is the opposite of verse, so it is not rhymes or poetry.

clue.text: Finally, you took the fourth option to reach high ground

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the next word

parts.note: after plans A, B and C comes plan D

explanation.surface: Someone, out of choices, took the fourth route to get to the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Plans A, B and C come first, so the fourth option is plan D.
explanation.definitionFit: Upland is elevated country, hills and moors, a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: A bit like Signor Antonio on the cause of depression

definitions.text: A bit like Signor Antonio on the cause of depression

indicators.note: a bit means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A comment on an Italian gentleman's views about why people feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'Signor Antonio'. Antonio in The Merchant of Venice opens the play saying 'I know not why I am so sad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio confesses he does not know why he is sad, so he is unaware of the reason for his gloom.

clue.text: Primate's big mistake

definitions.meaning: a kind of South American monkey known for its loud call

explanation.surface: An ape's or a churchman's blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a loud-calling monkey and a glaring blunder, two senses of one word.

clue.text: For instance, naked lady — extremely affectionate

indicators.note: extremely picks the extremes, the first and last letters, of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone cites a nude woman as an example of something very warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters of For, instance, naked and lady: FR, IE, ND, LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone warm and kindly towards you is loving, the same as affectionate.
